calls.video_title: Down 98%, Is it Finally Time to Buy Chargepoint Stock? | CHPT Stock Analysis
calls.price_at_call: $8 (stated current, up 11% today); DCF fair value rendered '$529' in auto-captions — read as $5.29 with the decimal dropped (same garbling renders forward price/sales '42' for 0.42), below the $8 price
calls.thesis: AVOID, first tracked Parkevtate CHPT call (no flip) — he reiterates a warning he has given for 5+ years and last on 15 Jun: ChargePoint is still not a buying opportunity even after falling over 98%, though it is getting closer. He has never ranked it a buy.
calls.base_case: Revenue is recovering ($433m trailing 12 months, with another growth quarter forecast) after management stopped growth-at-any-cost and fixed unit economics; the latest quarter was essentially cash-flat, and operating cash flow/sales improved from -65% to -16% on a trailing basis.
calls.bull_case: If ChargePoint can stay cash-flat until revenue growth accelerates into positive free cash flow (his DCF: free-cash-flow break-even in fiscal 2028, positive from fiscal 2029), it avoids further dilutive raises; persistently higher oil prices and faster EV adoption outside the US (Europe, China, South-East Asia; the US is only 6 of 100 new buyers) support charging demand.
calls.bear_case: Cash has dwindled from over $600m to just over $95m against over $227m of debt — more than the market capitalisation; a return to historic burn rates would force dilutive raises or desperate, high-rate borrowing, and even after a margin of safety his DCF still leaves the stock overvalued at $8.
